results.title: Soil moisture monitoring to support irrigation scheduling | OSU Extension Service
results.description:
### Tensiometers

Tensiometers are soil moisture sensors used to measure soil water tension (matric potential). Producers in horticultural, vegetable and specialty crop systems commonly use tensiometers where irrigation is frequent and soils are monitored closely.

#### How they work

A tensiometer (Figure 4) consists of:

 A water-filled tube approximately 1 inch in diameter
 A vacuum gauge, at the upper end
 A porous ceramic cup, at the lower end [...] For additional guidance on installation and operation, see Tensiometers: Installation and Operation.

results.title: Irrigation Management and Crop Characteristics of Alfalfa
results.description:
The matric potential reading will increase as the soil becomes drier. After the field is irrigated, the matric potential readings typically return to lower values (i.e., 0 to 10 kPa). These wetting and drying cycles continue throughout the season as the crop is irrigated and the soil dries with crop water use and surface soil evaporation. The key to proper irrigation management using soil water sensors is to monitor the sensors regularly, track the soil water level, and irrigate when the [...] irrigate when the kilopascal (1 kPa = 1 cbar) readings are in the desired range for your soil type (See Table I; Orloff et al., 2001). Irrigating when the soil water readings exceed the desired range may result in crop stress and yield loss. requirements.missing: No supplied document documents the specific soil moisture measurement method (tensiometer, FDR, TDR, gypsum block), a trigger threshold in original units, and a documented operational sequence showing how a farmer or automated system acts on that reading versus a fixed calendar schedule. Tables in s11/s13/s18 list threshold values but do not describe the measurement method, decision protocol, or system actuation.

While s17 explicitly names Medicago sativa L. and s11/s13 include alfalfa-specific tables, none of the supplied documents is fetched as directly relevant evidence specifically answering the alfalfa irrigation-scheduling-by-soil-moisture question; the threshold tables lack the method-and-decision context required, and no fetched document independently establishes crop-identity proof for the reader's question.

No supplied document provides measured soil moisture values with original units (kPa/cbar/%VWC) together with a clear distinction between crop evapotranspiration (ETc) and applied irrigation water volume, plus growth-stage or season adjustments to the threshold. S11 provides MAD/kPa thresholds but does not separately quantify ETc versus applied water, and no document documents stage-specific threshold adjustments for alfalfa.
